title: Counting the Crows
blurb: Akbar wants every crow in Delhi counted. Birbal already knows.
script:
[warmly] Long, long ago… in the great city of Delhi, there lived an emperor named Akbar. His palace had marble floors, and fountains that sparkled in the sun… and his court was full of wise ministers. [gently] But the wisest of them all, and the quickest to smile… was a man named Birbal.

[amused] Emperor Akbar LOVED to test Birbal. He would ask him riddles. He would ask him impossible questions. [short pause] And somehow… every single time… Birbal found an answer.

[calmly] One morning, Akbar stood by his tall palace window, looking out over the city. Below him, the rooftops of Delhi stretched as far as he could see. [curious] And on those rooftops… sat crows. Black, shiny crows. Crows hopping. Crows cawing. Crows… EVERYWHERE.

[thoughtful] The Emperor watched them for a long, long while.

[short pause] Then a funny thought came into his head. [mischievously] It was the kind of thought only an emperor would DARE to say out loud.

[excited] “Birbal!” he called. “Come here at once! I have a task for you.”

[calmly] Birbal came and bowed. “Yes, Your Majesty?”

[grandly] “Look at all these crows,” said Akbar, waving his hand at the window. “I want to know how many there are. Count them, Birbal. Tell me EXACTLY how many crows live in our city of Delhi.”

[surprised] The whole court went quiet. [whispers] The ministers looked at one another. [incredulous] Count the crows? Crows FLY! Crows NEVER sit still! You might count three… and by the time you counted the fourth… the first three would be GONE. [firmly] It was impossible. Everyone knew it was impossible.

[short pause] Everyone… [slyly] except Birbal.

[calmly] Birbal did not look worried at all. He stroked his beard… and smiled… as if the Emperor had asked him something easy, like the color of the sky.

“Your Majesty,” he said calmly, “I have already counted them.”

[surprised] Akbar’s eyebrows shot UP. “Already?!”

[cheerfully] “Oh yes,” said Birbal. [slowly] “There are exactly… sixty thousand… five hundred… and fifty… TWO crows in Delhi.”

[astonished] “Sixty thousand, five hundred and fifty-two!” the Emperor repeated. [thoughtful] The number was so quick, and so exact, that for a moment… he did not know what to say. [short pause] But Akbar was clever too. And he saw a way to catch his minister. [slyly] He leaned forward on his throne.

[mischievously] “Veeery well, Birbal,” he said with a sly smile. “But what if I ask my soldiers to count every crow… one by one? What if they find MORE crows than that? Hmm? What then?”

[calmly] “Ah,” said Birbal, “that is simple, Your Majesty. [brightly] If there are more, it means crows from OTHER towns have come to Delhi… to visit their friends and relatives. [amused] Guests, Your Majesty! Even crows have guests.”

[chuckles] The Emperor laughed. [playfully] But he was not finished. “And if my soldiers find FEWER crows? What will you say THEN?”

[cheerfully] “Even simpler,” said Birbal, with a little bow. “If there are fewer… it means some of our Delhi crows have flown away, to visit their OWN friends and relatives in other towns. [warmly] Crows have family everywhere, Your Majesty. They do LOVE to visit.”

[short pause] For a moment… the court was silent. Then Emperor Akbar threw back his head… and LAUGHED. [laughs heartily] And the whole court laughed with him. [amused] Nobody could ever count all the crows. And nobody… could EVER prove Birbal wrong.

[warmly] “Birbal,” said the Emperor, wiping his eyes, “I asked you an impossible question… and you gave me an impossible answer. [gently] It is… perfect.”

[softly] And from that day on, whenever Akbar looked out of his window and saw the crows on the rooftops of Delhi… he would smile, and think of his clever minister. [slowly] The minister who could answer any question in the world. [long pause] [whispers] Even a question… with wings.
